comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 appendix defines a 150-ECTS Mathematics major and 30-ECTS minor. Year 1 is a compulsory 60-ECTS common Mathematics/Applied Mathematics foundation, instantiated with First-year Project Mathematics because it directly represents the named degree. The second- and third-year major contributes 90 ECTS. Dynamical Systems and Algebraic Structures are selected as the first two options in their regulated choice group; Project Statistical Reasoning is selected as the first option in the subsequent group; and Project Systems Theory is the first listed eligible elective. These choices are fixed by official order independently of UCR fit. The genuine 30-ECTS minor remains open rather than being populated with invented courses. Rechecked against the current official programme and 2026–2027 regulations on 2026-10-14; the settled 180-ECTS reconstruction and neutral choices are unchanged.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The historical no-match judgment imposed full disciplinary equivalence. The strongest feasible response is a mathematics-and-computation curriculum, and the explicit probability interest supports one genuinely different statistical-research route. A third pure-mathematics direction was assessed but cannot form a complete UCR programme because the workbook lacks the target’s proof sequence in real and functional analysis, topology, group theory, geometry, number theory and advanced algebra, as well as comparable disciplinary project supervision. No further generator-eligible direction remains.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address professional and societal responsibility; UCR PPD is general formation rather than mathematics-specific ethics.
Both develop statistical modelling; UCR applies multivariate models in behavioural research rather than mathematical statistics.
Both develop programming for problem-solving; UCR teaches general Python rather than a mathematics-specific scientific-programming course.
Both use logic, sets and discrete structures; UCR applies them to algorithms rather than providing the full proof-based target course.
Both establish calculus and equation-solving foundations; UCR also introduces complex numbers and differential equations.
Both directly study systems, vectors, matrices and linear spaces; Groningen continues to a second dedicated course.
Both establish probability distributions; UCR combines probability with statistical inference and simulation.
Both study numerical root-finding, interpolation, differentiation, integration and differential-equation methods with attention to error.
Both analyse linear systems through transforms, differential equations and state-space representations.
Both extend calculus; UCR includes multivariable and complex-valued functions but not the target analysis sequence.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes are bounded related-field responses. They cover mathematical methods, computation, probability and quantitative research, but do not reproduce Groningen’s cumulative proof-based pure-mathematics curriculum in analysis, topology, group theory, geometry, number theory and algebraic structures or its 15-EC Mathematics research project.
